_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `dag.dag` is a semio-NATIVE port-directed computation graph whose nodes and edges live in a composed `s.stdio.semio.graph` child, so no oracle is registered and the evidence rests on the committed per-kind rejection vectors plus the inverse law over the real committed example document (see noOracleDecisions).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third party reads or writes `.dag.dsl.semio`/`.dag.pack.semio`, and no graph library holds an opinion about the two things this vocabulary actually decides. First, `DagSnapshot` persists NO nodes and NO edges: it carries `schema` plus one composed `s.stdio.semio.graph` child handle whose `childId` is a content digest of the child, so what an applied mutation produces is a NEW handle and what a refused one produces is the same handle — an addressing scheme private to this repository. Second, the vocabulary is a DAG vocabulary, not a graph one: `connect-nodes` refuses a self-loop and refuses any edge whose target can already reach its source (`🔗connect-nodes/🔺️diff/🦀️component.rs::would_create_cycle`), and endpoints are `node@port` strings split by this plugin's own `split_endpoint`. A general graph crate asked to adjudicate either would be answering a different question. Confidence comes instead from the fourteen committed, independently handcrafted specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — one per kind, each already unit-tested inside the production crate itself — and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property. Those fourteen vectors are ALL rejection vectors, and deliberately so: the leaf tests state the reason in as many words (`🌱create-node/🧪️tests/rejects-a-duplicate-node-id/🦀️component.rs`) — hand-authoring an APPLIED `➡️after` would mean hand-forging a `std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher` digest, a value the standard library explicitly does not specify. `mutate-dag-1` therefore runs each vector for its exact `(code, severity, target)` triple AND separately applies a real-effect payload of its own to the committed five-node example document, where the content-addressed handle supplies the observability the vectors cannot.
